limitations: All 2939 records remain in the overall investigation; this is a seven-term follow-up, not whole-record completion.
The four selected primary reviews do not establish a complete phenotype or exact allele crosswalk.
Reviewed-only Mex and ini searches are reference queries, not exhaustive unreviewed-protein searches.
Reference-strain taxids are not automatically experimental-isolate identifiers.
The fungal MDR1 family remains without a single selected organism or protein; its descendants are not propagated.
Source assertions and all earlier curated findings remain unchanged. No exact experimental protein, allele, genome or new AST is assigned.
No sequences, exact variants, constructs, primers, protocols, coordinates or numerical AST are exported.
No NCBI endpoint requests, outreach, source adoption or GitHub mutations occurred; #1040 remains deferred.

PMID:10515918.finding: The named system comprises distinct protein components; its regulator is not one of those components. The study distinguishes reference/background and experimental subjects.
PMID:10515918.limit: A PAO1 reference accession does not identify every tested subject or the whole complex. No experimental phenotype or allele is added.
locations: Discussion: scope of the regulator study

PMID:10639358.finding: The authors explicitly distinguish cohort association from proof that the observed changes cause resistance.
PMID:10639358.limit: The cited study does not validate an exact ini allele by reference-protein identity. Distinct strain references are not interchangeable, and no causal efflux route is newly inferred.

PMID:20547810.finding: CAGL0G00242g is aligned with the historical YOR1 name in the gene-annotation table; the annotation's homology basis remains explicit.
PMID:20547810.limit: This supports reference nomenclature, not a clinical isolate's protein accession, exact allele, or a posaconazole-specific causal claim.
locations: Table 4: gene annotation and homology footnote

PMID:35038899.finding: Gene-level susceptibility findings depend on biological context and are distinguished from direct drug transport.
PMID:35038899.limit: This independently discovered follow-up does not identify the ontology's posaconazole-associated allele. A drug-specific transport observation is not generalized to every azole.
locations: Discussion: gene-level functional interpretation and stated limitations
